fixes.new:
A national idol who climbed to her current status in barely a year since her debut.
She is active across many fields - major entertainment company Zolbrain's flagship games, commercials for Kerdonald Foods, and the cover of the magazine 'Monthly: A Man's Cooking', which $$ジョニー$$ himself subscribes to, among others.
She once lost out on a commercial appearance to $$ジョニー$$'s business skill, and since then took an interest in him, going so far as to gather information about him online. Eventually, at a party hosted by Igor Konzern, she meets $$ジョニー$$ in person, and the two grow drawn to each other.
Her true identity is the pilot of the R-Daigan.
Her catchphrase is 'I'm going to make this happen!'
Acting on $$ウラジミール$$'s orders, she repeatedly clashed with Team D. Eventually, right after she prompts the activation of the God Beast Mode, her assigned role, she is utterly beaten down, but her life is saved by $$ジョニー$$, who was quick to realize her true identity.
In the later battle against the Unknown, she shows outstanding teamwork with Team D, and when the team heads for the moon, she officially becomes one of its members.
After the final battle on the moon, with peace restored, she was seen enjoying shopping in the city with $$ジョニー$$.
fixes.reason: mistranslation: the Japanese says she urges/prompts the activation of the God Beast Mode (that is her role); the English reversed it so that she is the one being prompted

fixes.new:
$$ドラゴンズハイヴ$$'s fourth-generation mental counselor. Fifteen years old.
Though young, she holds over one hundred licenses in psychiatry and psychology, and intensely dislikes being treated like a child. Incidentally, in Japan, where she lives, the age of adulthood is fifteen, and she insists at every opportunity that she is '15 years and 3 months old'.
She also dislikes having her name shortened to 'Ruriruri', and is put in a bad mood whenever someone calls her that.
Despite being a counselor, she is not good with men, and brings along a guard robot whenever she counsels $$ジョニー$$ or $$朔哉$$.
Beyond counseling, she is also skilled at piloting robots and the like.
fixes.reason: mistranslation: the shortened form in the Japanese is Ruriruri, not her surname Riruri; 'Riruri' would not be a shortening of Ruu Riruri

fixes.new:
$$ドラゴンズハイヴ$$'s chief mechanic.
She is a humanist who shows equal affection not only to the machines but to the pilots who operate them.
She also has strong analytical skills and is reliable in many situations, but her one flaw is that she is a bad drunk. Once drunk, she loses all sense of gender boundaries, and has even pounced on $$葵$$.
As for machines, she does not just maintain them but also develops new weapons, and it was at $$朔哉$$'s request that she fitted the Boost Nova Knuckle.
fixes.reason: mistranslation: the Japanese says bad drinking habits (a bad drunk), not low tolerance; the Japanese verb means attacked/pounced on, not made a pass

fixes.new:
The developer of the R-Daigan.
She is also the one who discovered and raised its pilot, $$エイーダ$$.
To secure funding, she has partnered with Zolbrain, a rival of Igor Konzern. She deftly manages the company president's wishes while keeping her own goals as his top priority.
She was once married to $$田中司令$$, and the two show a love-hate relationship, greeting each other with a slap followed by a kiss.
Incidentally, the design data for the R-Daigan was sent by WILL; $$ウラジミール$$ did not build it entirely from scratch.
fixes.reason: pronoun: Vladimir is female; pronoun: Vladimir is female (ex-spouse of Commander Tanaka)

fixes.new:
A journalist affiliated with BWC.
She harbors suspicions about the Dancouga Nova's actions and existence, and is known as the 'combat correspondent' for flying into battlefields without regard for her own safety.
She won a Pulitzer Prize for her collected reporting, titled 'Is the Dancouga Necessary on the Battlefield?'
As she continues her activities, she comes under pressure from above, but holds firm to her conviction and keeps reporting regardless.
Eventually, her overreaching actions bring pressure down on the entire mass media industry, but she leaves her company rather than stop reporting. With information provided by $$朔哉$$, whom she met at a party hosted by Igor Konzern, she gradually closes in on the truth.
When WILL personally reveals the whole truth, she speaks as though she has given up on turning it into an article. But her resolve to keep covering the Dancouga as long as she lives never wavers, and she accompanies the team to the final battle on the moon, witnessing everything to the end.
After the fighting over the Dancouga came to an end, unable to suppress her journalistic instincts after all, she continued reporting on WILL.
fixes.reason: mistranslation: the title says on the battlefield (senjou), not 'the World'

fixes.new:
A sniper from $$リットナー村$$.
She has a realistic, level-headed side, but also an honest, cheerful, straightforward personality, and could be called the mood-maker of $$大グレン団$$ - though as the years passed, she grew into a woman with added composure and warmth.
She handles a sniper rifle bigger than she is with ease, and her marksmanship, which she confidently claimed was the best in the village, has not dulled in the slightest.
After the new government was established, feeling it was not her place, she left her comrades and traveled alone to $$コレハナ島$$, where she took the name $$ヨマコ$$ and became a teacher.
As the world faces a new crisis, she resolves to fight for the sake of the children and rejoins $$大グレン団$$. She rescues $$シモン$$ and $$ヴィラル$$ from their peril in prison, then heads out into space and fights against the $$アンチスパイラル$$.
fixes.reason: mistranslation: the Japanese says the shooting skill she herself claimed/believed was the village's best, not a source of pride for the village

fixes.new:
The first princess of the Spiral King $$ロージェノム$$.
During the battle against the Spiral King, she emerges from a container $$シモン$$ discovers, and joins $$大グレン団$$ as she is.
She is naive to an astonishing degree, with an extremely pure, easygoing personality. Moreover, as the enemy commander's daughter, the members of $$大グレン団$$, who had just lost $$カミナ$$, are at first cold toward her. But her charm and strength of will win over everyone's hearts, and she becomes something of an idol figure to the group. She has a particularly great influence on $$シモン$$'s growth.
During the decisive battle inside $$テッペリン$$, she rides along in $$ラガン$$ and fights alongside $$シモン$$. After witnessing her father $$ロージェノム$$'s defeat, she speaks of her resolve to move toward tomorrow.
Her cooking skill is so bizarre it traumatizes $$ロシウ$$. Only $$シモン$$ (and $$ブータ$$) seem to find it delicious, and that remains true even now.
Eventually she accepts $$シモン$$'s proposal, but at first, in a moment of obliviousness, turns him down. But after seriously reconsidering what it meant, she accepts. Just as the two seem destined to be joined together, however, the $$アンチスパイラル$$ factor dormant within her awakens, and she becomes a Messenger.
After the battle against the $$アンチスパイラル$$, she holds a wedding ceremony with $$シモン$$, who saved her. Right after they exchange a kiss, because she is a virtual life form, she vanishes along with the fall of the $$アンチスパイラル$$. But her final moment is one of savoring her happiness, with a smile on her face.
fixes.reason: mistranslation: the Japanese says the members found her off-putting/shunned her, not merely 'wary'

fixes.new:
A science bureau official of the New Government.
He once served as a lookout aboard Dai-Gurren, but now works a desk job; constant all-nighters have left him with permanent bags under his eyes. On top of that, his lack of exercise these days has left him considerably heavier.
When the Team Dai-Gurren members departed for space, he supported those around him as an operator, working as hard as ever.
fixes.reason: addition: 'them' and 'from behind the scenes' are not in the Japanese (supported those around him, as an operator, with unchanged effort)

fixes.new:
An operator in the New Government's Defense Operations Room.
Like $$ギンブレー$$ and others, she belongs to a younger generation than the members of $$大グレン団$$ who fought in the war against the Spiral King.
Her skill in accurately directing operations against the movements of the $$ムガン$$ that appeared in $$カミナシティ$$ was recognized, and she was entrusted with operator duties aboard both the $$アークグレン$$ and the $$超銀河ダイグレン$$.
fixes.reason: mistranslation: the Japanese says the Mugann's actions/movements (koudou), not 'the appearance'

fixes.new:
The indomitable, ferocious leader of $$グレン団$$.
An overwhelmingly forceful man, he powers through anything with sheer spirit and momentum, kicking reason aside to make the impossible happen.
His recklessness was legendary: he once faced down a Gunmen armed with nothing but a sword. He went on to steal a Gunmen bare-handed and pilot it on the spot, and drove $$ラガン$$ into $$グレン$$'s head to declare a 'combination,' then made it a reality, displaying his free-spirited, wild nature at every turn.
Yet his fighting spirit, force of will, and conviction to see anything through gave him tremendous charisma. When he left $$ジーハ村$$, his only companions were $$シモン$$ and $$ヨーコ$$, but he drew in everyone he met, eventually building $$大グレン団$$ into a great force.
He and $$ヨーコ$$, both strong-willed, never stopped bickering over trivial things. Still, they cared for each other, and before the decisive battle against $$チミルフ$$ they opened their hearts and shared a kiss. He boasted, 'I'll pay you back tenfold when I get back,' but a mistake by $$シモン$$ during the battle proved the trigger for a fatal wound. With his last ounce of strength he scolded $$シモン$$ and passed his soul on to him, then burned away to pure white.
Both his way of living and his way of dying left their mark on countless people, and even on the Beastmen.
A statue of $$カミナ$$ stands in the city of '$$カミナシティ$$,' built on the site of $$テッペリン$$.
When $$大グレン団$$ was trapped in the multiverse labyrinth by the $$アンチスパイラル$$, he appeared before $$シモン$$ and $$ヨーコ$$ and gave each of them the push they needed.
fixes.reason: mistranslation: kessen = decisive battle, not 'final battle' (this is far from the game's final battle); 'finally' is not in the Japanese

fixes.new:
An EVA pilot.
Born in England, she belongs to the Euro Branch of the special agency $$ＮＥＲＶ$$.
Known for her red-framed glasses and a speech habit of sometimes tacking 'nya' onto the ends of sentences. She has an optimistic personality, but $$加持$$ calls her a 'problem child.' At the $$ベタニアベース$$, she piloted the $$ＥＶＡ仮設５号機$$ and fought the Third Angel.
She later visits $$第３新東京市$$, where she sniffs out the faint scent of L.C.L. clinging to $$シンジ$$ and nicknames him '$$ＮＥＲＶ$$'s little puppy.' Her words and actions are eccentric, and much about her remains a mystery.
fixes.reason: omission: tokidoki (sometimes) was missing; tense: 'rode ... and fought' is a completed past event (the next sentence says she LATER visits Tokyo-3); 'to fight' also turned a sequence into a purpose

fixes.new:
A mysterious boy at the lunar $$タブハベース$$.
He speaks and acts as though he knows $$シンジ$$.
fixes.reason: addition/mistranslation: 'is at' not 'stationed'; the Japanese says he behaves AS IF he knew Shinji, not 'suggest he somehow already knows'
